claims.statement: For every ordinary arity-2,3,4 path-star profile and represented branch i, A0-Ai=z^3 F_(r_i) H_i, so Delta_p A0-Delta_p Ai=Delta_(p-3)(F_(r_i)H_i). Therefore branch i is strictly selected exactly when this cofactor difference exceeds Delta_p A0.
claims.scope: All m>=1 ordinary path-stars with distinct branches of arity in {2,3,4}, integer zero-extended coefficients, and every natural current rank p. The identity is branchwise and does not erase original tip-tag multiplicities in any aggregate.
claims.reason: Direct expansion proves the polynomial identity; zero-extended coefficient shifting gives the stated difference identity and strict selector equivalence.

claims.statement: A census-free proof that an endpoint-selected eligible row always has at least one represented branch i with Delta_(p-3)(F_(r_i)H_i)>Delta_p A0 would exclude endpoint-only selection on this family.
claims.scope: Reduction at actual eligible lower-half ranks only, retaining x as the least strict zero-extended parent descent including the terminal difference, x+2<=p, 3p<2alpha+1, 2p<=alpha, j=p-2, current-p strict flags, and original private-tip multiplicities. No universal crossing assertion is proved here.
claims.reason: The conditional implication follows exactly from the strict threshold identity. The existence of a crossing in every eligible endpoint-selected row remains unproved; the bounded row only refutes a nonnegative-slope shortcut.

The exact coefficients and slopes are in the report and replay output. This refutes only the shortcut requiring a nonnegative slope.

limitations: No census-free universal endpoint-only exclusion proof was established.
The exact row is bounded evidence against the nonnegative-slope shortcut only, not an endpoint-only witness or primary payment counterexample.
